full_judgment:
3. Mr Helaluddin Mollah, learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the State, did not dispute the legal point agitated by the learned Advocate, Mr. Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, but he submits that a direction may be given to dispose of the case expeditiously. 

 5. We have perused the Rule petition along with annexures. An first information report was lodged against the accused petitioners by Sub-Inspector of Police Md Abdul Wahab on 9-2-2002 alleging that the accused petitioners murdered Mst Sabana, wife of accused Abdul Jabbar. The father of the deceased filed an application before the learned Magistrate for treating the case as Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Case and prayed for inclusion of the accused petitioners with Abdul Jabbar as accuseds to the said case. Learned Magistrate by order dated 20-2-2002 passed an order for filing the case in proper forum. Against which Criminal Revision No. 62 of 2002 was taken before the learned Sessions Judge and the learned Sessions Judge ordered the application filed by the father of the deceased to be treated as statement under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in the case. Police after investigation submitted charge sheet on 1-5-2002 against Abdul Jabbar under section 302 of the Penal Code against which, the father of the deceased, Md Matiur Rahman Chowdhury filed a naraji petition. Learned Magistrate by order dated 25-6-2002 allowed the naraji petition and sent the case for further investigation. Police after, investigation filed a supplementary charge sheet on 27-8-2002 on a white paper. We find reinvestigation was made by the police and another supplementary charge sheet was filed on 21-9-2002. The learned Magistrate accepted the supplementary charge sheet where- upon the accused petitioners voluntarily surrendered and obtained bail from this court in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 4737 of 2003 on 13-4-2003. Against acceptance of supplementary. charge sheet, the father of the victim moved the learned Sessions Judge in Criminal Revision No. 209 of 2002. The learned Sessions Judge by the impugned order allowed the revision and passed the following order; 

 "Since the record lies with the present Court it does not require to send the record to the lower Court. We now take cognisance of the aforesaid offence against the accuseds named in the complaint petition namely, 1. Md A Jabbar, 2. Md A Aziz Master, 3. Gafuran Bibi, 4. A Jalil, 5. Monoara, 6. Amzad Hossain, 7. Najrul Islam, 8. Shahjahan and at the same time we do make our direction to register the Sessions Case 248/2002 as the case under Nari-o-Shishu Nirjajtan Daman Ain, 2000 and issue warrant against the rest accuseds. The, revision case is accordingly, disposed of." 

 6. It is settled principle of law that naraji is a fresh complaint. The order passed by the learned Sessions Judge taking cognisance in revision arisen from naraji petition has no support of law as it is the duty of the learned Magistrate to take cognisance of the case and by this impugned order, learned Sessions Judge usurped the jurisdiction of the learned Magistrate which law does not permit him to do. Proper course opened was to send the case record to the learned Magistrate after allowing the revision with a direction to examine the complainant and thereafter, the learned Magistrate, if he thinks fit, to take cognisance of the case against the accused petitioners. Section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure does not say taking of cognisance by the Sessions Judge in revision. The entire order passed by the learned Sessions Judge is without jurisdiction and calls for interference. We find substance in this Rule. 

 The learned Sessions Judge is directed to send the case records to the learned Magistrate so that the learned Magistrate can take proper steps as per observations made in the body of the judgment. The order taking cognisance by the learned Sessions Judge is quashed.
